tasks.title: No black flashes on restore or section switch
tasks.body: Steven recorded a video: restoring the window from the Windows taskbar paints the whole window solid black first, then every text label, card and sidebar item shows as a solid black box for a moment before its content draws. The same black-box flashing happens when switching sections (Devices, Monitor, Fans, Profiles, ...). Earlier fixes (b1ec458, fix-restore-flicker) did not solve it on the real PC.
tasks.assignment: Branch: fix-repaint-black. Find and fix the cause of both black flashes. Start with: App._on_unmap/_on_map and the restore path in central_rgb.py; the page switch that uses fx.freeze/fx.thaw (WM_SETREDRAW + RedrawWindow with RDW_ERASE) around self._holder; tk.Frame/Canvas widgets whose bg or the window class background brush is black or unset; the DWM title-bar/glass calls and alpha changes in win_effects.py; and whether pages are destroyed and rebuilt on switch instead of being kept and raised. Fix it so the window keeps showing its last frame (or the panel colour, never black) until the new content is drawn, for example: give the root and every container an explicit P['BG']/P['CARD'] background, drop RDW_ERASE or erase with the panel brush, keep built pages and raise them instead of rebuilding, and repaint once after restore. Do not restyle anything. Verify with tests/preview.py and tests/restore_check.py under Xvfb (minimize/restore and rapid section switching), capturing frames during the restore and the switch; add tests/test_repaint.py that fails if any captured frame during restore or switch contains large near-black regions where the theme has no black, and that every container widget has a non-default background. tasks.title: Settings: Dark / Light appearance toggle
tasks.body: Steven asked for a dark/light theme toggle on the Settings page. Today every theme in central_rgb.py THEMES is dark and ctk.set_appearance_mode('dark') is hard-coded.
tasks.assignment: Branch: feat-theme-toggle. Add an Appearance setting with two choices, Dark and Light, as a Windows 11-style row on the Settings page next to the existing theme dropdown (reuse the existing settings row helper). Save it as settings['appearance'] = 'dark' | 'light'; a missing or unknown value means dark, so older settings files load unchanged. Give every entry in THEMES (and the default gunmetal SOLID palette) a light variant: light BG/SIDE/CARD/CARD2/LINE/TEXT/MUTED/TRACK/HOVER/SEL/BTN values, keeping each theme's accent hue but darkened enough for readable contrast on light panels (aim for WCAG AA 4.5:1 for body text; use the existing readable-text helper for text on accent colours). Apply it through _apply_theme (e.g. _apply_theme(key, appearance)) and the existing live rebuild in _switch_theme, so flipping the toggle repaints the window in place with no restart and lighting, fans, sensors and OpenRGB keep running. Set ctk.set_appearance_mode to match, and make win_effects use a light title bar in light mode (failing quietly off Windows). Tests: add tests/test_appearance.py covering: default is dark when the key is missing; every theme has a complete light palette (all SOLID keys present, valid hex); body text vs card contrast is at least 4.5:1 in light mode for every theme; toggling through the harness rebuilds the Settings page without errors and persists the value. Add a light-mode option to tests/preview.py (e.g. --appearance light) and capture Home, Lighting, Fans, Monitor and Settings in light mode. RULES FOR THIS TASK: Follow CLAUDE.md.
